description.narrative: Multidimensional and multisectoral crisis in the Tillabéri region of Niger (security, climate, food and nutrition) For more than a decade, the Tillabéry region, located in the tri-border area (Burkina Faso - Mali - Niger), has been the scene of atrocities perpetrated by armed terrorist groups (GATs). This violence takes the form of targeted attacks on civilians, raids on villages, assaults ondefense and security forces, and damage to local infrastructure.Faced with this persistent insecurity, thousandsof people have beenforced to abandon their homelands, fleeing the threat to take refuge in localities deemed safer. This phenomenon of forced displacement exacerbates the pressure on host areas, where resources remain limited and access to essential services such as food, water, health and education is becoming increasingly critical.The December 2024 Cadre Harmonisé (CH) reveals a worrying food security situation in the region of Tillabéry, Niger. Currently, 549,630 people (12% of the regional population) require urgent food assistance, while the projection for the lean season 2025 estimates that this figure could rise to 767,439 people (17% of the population). The departments of Ouallam and Gothéye are among the worst affected areas, with 91,295 and 66,520 people respectively classified as severelyfood insecure. During the lean season, the most vulnerable households are forced to adopt detrimental survival strategies, such as drastically cutting back on meals, selling essential goods, or forcing people to migrate to supposedly more favorable areas. A largepart (40%) of this Catfund will be used by Niger to cover human resource gaps on the humanitarian component. It should be noted that 60% of this grant will be used to provide food assistance during the 2025 lean season to 200 households from vulnerable communities (IDPs, hosts and refugees) in the GFFO2 project intervention zone as co-matching.Preferably, the start date of this grant is set for June 15, 2024, with a closing date of March 31, 2026 (i.e. 10 months in total), to give countries a little more leeway and enablethem to cover the entire lean season.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education for all, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam Novibs main office is based in The Netherlands, it supports the work of a network of local offices, the implementation of global projects, fund raising, campaigning and advocacy. The Hub Niamey Niger exists since 2006 as a humanitarian field office and since 2012 as the decentralized Country office for Oxfam Novib, dealing with all the development and humanitarian themes like Sustainable livelihoods, Right to Basic services, Humanitarian and resilience interventions, The right to be heard and the right to an Identity, including women's rights and sexual and reproductive health rights. The Country Office in Niger works with local partners to realize the vision of a Niger without poverty
